description: Northern Thai lantern: a ribbed cloth-over-bamboo drum with a scalloped skirt, hung at temples and during Yi Peng

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Hanging lantern built as a tall drum of stretched cloth over a frame, its sides bulging gently and divided by raised vertical ribs into broad panels, a flat circular cap closing the top with a short stiff hanging loop standing up from it, a narrow band collar around the drum at the bottom, and below that a short stiff skirt of wide scalloped tabs standing out in a ring, each tab a solid tapered flap rather than a loose strand Materials: Ivory and gold cloth with a saffron-yellow band, the weave visible and the colour sun-faded and blotched with damp on one side, gold foil trim on the ribs and collar rubbed thin, dust and cobwebs along the top cap, the skirt tabs creased and dog-eared.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.441 x 0.721 x 0.441 m. Cost: 1872 triangles / 4000, 2 draw calls / 4, 2 materials / 3, 2 unique geometries / 6, 0 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.998, 0.997, 0.997], interior hole fractions [0.0001, 0.0033, 0.0038, 0.0035]).  Two components at 2 draw calls, 2 materials and 2 geometries against a large ceiling of 4/3/6; the ribs and pleats are where the 1872 triangles go.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.441 x 0.721 x 0.441 m against the declared 0.42 x 0.72 x 0.42 -- exact on height, 5% over on width and depth, the overshoot being the skirt's pleat crests standing proud of the drum's r 0.21. Against the plate the drum is a little squatter and the skirt a little wider than ideal, which is the honest residual.

A stiff twenty-pleat fan at 30 mm amplitude over a profile that flares to r 0.214 and TURNS BACK UP at the hem, which is what gives the folded lip the plate shows. The previous build hung a smooth ellipsoid there. It also had to reach up to the drum's foot band: at its first position a 75 mm gap opened between drum and skirt that you could see straight through, where the plate's skirt hangs directly off the band.

Twenty ribs running the drum's full height as a modulation around the axis, tinted toward a darker cream at the troughs. A lathe is constant around its own axis and cannot carry them, which is why both drum and skirt are ribbedDomes -- forty folds for two submissions. The previous build had a plain cylinder with a few loose gold sticks standing beside it.

Two material layers: cream cloth at luma 186 carrying its rib troughs as a vertex colour, and gilt trim at luma 150 for the cap, the three gathering bands and the hanging wire. Both sit far above gatecrop's erased 55.5-60.5 window, so unlike this kit's dark props neither needed a tone correction. Roughness 0.90 on the cloth -- matt, with no specular band that could rise into the window. NOT carried: the plate's gold rib TAPES, which are applied strips over the cloth rather than the tinted troughs used here.

name: Lanna Cloth Hanging Lantern
notes:
The northern Thai temple lantern (โคมล้านนา), hung in ranks along temple eaves and through Chiang Mai during Yi Peng -- distinct from the round red Chinese lantern in that it is a tall ribbed drum with a stiff scalloped skirt rather than a plump barrel with a tassel. Sized as a 0.42 m drum with the skirt bringing the hang to 0.72 m; the height figure is the fixture and skirt, not the cord, because the cord belongs to whatever it hangs from. The skirt is authored as a ring of solid tapered tabs rather than a fringe deliberately: fringed geometry is what the reference reconstruction loses and what costs a low-end GPU its frame. Pivot is top-center so it hangs from the fixing loop. Static: hung, so physics stays disabled.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED medium -> large (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
